convention-probe.title: convention-probe
convention-probe.author: gwendall, chipvoice project
convention-probe.purpose: INIT's own calling convention: A, X, Y and PHP-pulled P, stored straight to $D400-$D403 once, read back as a write-stream instead of inferred from the file format document's prose. X and Y are never scored against the oracle (see compare.mjs's own ignoreAddrs): the format spec never defines them, chipvoice deliberately zeroes them, and libsidplayfp's own reference driver leaves them holding whatever incidental value an unrelated setup branch happened to load - see docs/chips/c64.md. A and P, and the whole PLAY phase that follows, are scored normally.

frame-rate-probe.title: frame-rate-probe
frame-rate-probe.author: gwendall, chipvoice project
frame-rate-probe.purpose: PLAY's own cadence: a start marker in INIT, then one INC $D400 every call, for many frames - whether PLAY is called once a frame, at the tune's declared speed, and how closely its cycle lands against a real per-line VIC-II's own raster IRQ.

gt2-dojo.title: Dojo
gt2-dojo.author: Cadaver (Lasse Öörni)
gt2-dojo.purpose: A real tune (2002, Covert Bitops) exported by a real tool's own command-line packer/relocator instead of a self-made probe: `examples/dojo.sng`, one of GoatTracker 2's own bundled example songs, run through `src/gt2reloc.c` (the GT2RELOC-guarded, non-interactive build of the same relocator the interactive editor's own F9 calls - `GT2RELOC=1 gt2reloc dojo.sng gt2-dojo.sid`, default settings) from the official v2.77 distribution (SourceForge, md5 fdfdae268284bc175d94b8978822567f, matching the project's own published RSS hash). PAL timing and a 1x speed multiplier make GoatTracker 2's own relocator write an all-zero PSID speed word: VBI-timed, called from the vertical blank rather than a CIA timer. Never HVSC, never a commercial rip (decision 41).

gt2-sanction-cia.title: On a sanction from CIA
gt2-sanction-cia.author: Cadaver (Lasse Öörni)
gt2-sanction-cia.purpose: The corpus's own CIA-timed half of the same real player: `examples/sanction.sng` (2005, Covert Bitops) through the same `gt2reloc` with `-S2` (a 2x speed multiplier, `GT2RELOC=1 gt2reloc sanction.sng gt2-sanction-cia.sid -S2`), which makes the relocator write an all-ones PSID speed word instead - CIA #1 timer-A-timed, not vertical-blank. Same driver, same tool, same distribution as gt2-dojo, only the timing source and the tune differ, so a real divergence here isolates the CIA path specifically. Never HVSC, never a commercial rip (decision 41).

gt2-hyperspace-alt.title: My Own Hyperspace
gt2-hyperspace-alt.author: :P
gt2-hyperspace-alt.purpose: The corpus's own second driver: `examples/hyperspace.sng` (2005) through `gt2reloc` with `-Af000` (`GT2RELOC=1 gt2reloc hyperspace.sng gt2-hyperspace-alt.sid -Af000`), which is the real, documented way gt2reloc's own hardrestart-ADSR flag selects `altplayer.s` (see greloc.c: `if (adparam >= 0xf000) playername = "altplayer.s"`) instead of the standard `player.s` used by gt2-dojo and gt2-sanction-cia - a second, structurally different real driver from the same bundled distribution, not a second copy of the first. PAL, 1x speed: VBI-timed. Never HVSC, never a commercial rip (decision 41).

gt2-consultant-alt-cia.title: The Consultant
gt2-consultant-alt-cia.author: Cadaver (Lasse Öörni)
gt2-consultant-alt-cia.purpose: The second driver's own CIA-timed half: `examples/consultant.sng` (2002, Covert Bitops) through `gt2reloc -Af000 -S2` (`GT2RELOC=1 gt2reloc consultant.sng gt2-consultant-alt-cia.sid -Af000 -S2`) - altplayer.s again, this time CIA #1-timed. Completes a 2 driver x 2 timing matrix (gt2-dojo, gt2-sanction-cia, gt2-hyperspace-alt, gt2-consultant-alt-cia) from one real, redistributable tool's own two bundled playroutines. Never HVSC, never a commercial rip (decision 41).
